questions.question_text: During glomerular filtration, which substance is normally retained in the blood because the filtration barrier excludes blood cells and most large plasma proteins?
questions.explanation: The glomerular filtration barrier normally retains blood cells and most large plasma proteins while allowing water and small solutes into the filtrate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Glucose is present in the filtrate entering a healthy nephron but is normally absent from final urine. Which process explains this?
questions.option_a: Selective tubular reabsorption, mainly in the proximal tubule
questions.option_b: Glucose is converted into urea in the bladder
questions.option_c: Glucose is secreted into the renal artery
questions.option_d: Filtration of glucose is completely prevented
questions.explanation: Glucose is filtered at the glomerulus and normally reabsorbed from the proximal tubule back into blood.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient with markedly elevated blood glucose begins excreting glucose in urine. What best explains this finding?
questions.option_a: The bladder converts glucose into protein
questions.option_b: The glomerulus has stopped filtering all water
questions.option_c: Filtered glucose load exceeds the tubules’ reabsorptive capacity
questions.option_d: The ureters secrete insulin into urine
questions.explanation: When filtered glucose exceeds the renal threshold and transport capacity, not all of it can be reabsorbed, producing glycosuria.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After release of antidiuretic hormone, the collecting ducts become more permeable to water. What change is expected?
questions.option_a: More water returns to blood and urine volume falls
questions.option_c: Urea production by the liver ceases
questions.option_d: Less water is reabsorbed and urine becomes more dilute
questions.explanation: ADH increases water permeability in collecting ducts, promoting water reabsorption and reducing urine volume.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Aldosterone acts on the distal nephron. Which paired effect is most consistent with its action?
questions.option_c: Increased glucose filtration and decreased sodium reabsorption
questions.option_d: Increased sodium reabsorption and increased potassium secretion
questions.explanation: Aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in distal nephron segments; water may follow sodium depending on conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In the loop of Henle, which segment is relatively impermeable to water while reabsorbing salts, helping build the medullary osmotic gradient?
questions.explanation: The ascending limb reabsorbs salts but is relatively impermeable to water, contributing to the kidney medulla’s osmotic gradient.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A histological section shows renal corpuscles in an outer region and long nephron loops extending toward an inner region. Which pairing names these regions correctly?
questions.explanation: Renal corpuscles are in the cortex, while loops of Henle and collecting ducts extend into the medulla.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A ureter is partly blocked by a calculus. Which immediate consequence is most likely upstream of the obstruction?
questions.option_a: Urine backs up and pressure may rise in the renal pelvis
questions.option_b: The bladder stops storing urine permanently
questions.explanation: Obstruction can impede urine flow, causing back-pressure and dilation of the collecting system (hydronephrosis).
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In haemodialysis, waste solutes such as urea leave blood mainly because they:
questions.option_a: Diffuse across a semipermeable membrane down a concentration gradient
questions.option_b: Are destroyed by red blood cells
questions.option_c: Are filtered by the patient’s lungs
questions.option_d: Are converted into glucose by the dialyser
questions.explanation: Dialysis uses diffusion across a semipermeable membrane; small waste solutes move from blood into dialysis fluid while cells and large proteins are retained.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The right kidney is often positioned slightly lower than the left in the abdomen. Which neighbouring organ chiefly accounts for this?
questions.explanation: The large liver occupies space above the right kidney, so the right kidney typically lies somewhat lower than the left.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When blood becomes too acidic, which renal response helps restore acid-base balance over time?
questions.option_c: Excrete all bicarbonate and retain all hydrogen ions
questions.option_d: Secrete more hydrogen ions and conserve or generate bicarbonate
questions.explanation: Kidneys regulate pH by secreting hydrogen ions and reabsorbing or generating bicarbonate; this response is slower than respiratory buffering.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A urine dipstick repeatedly detects substantial albumin in a patient without strenuous exercise. Which kidney structure is a likely site of abnormal leakage?
questions.explanation: Persistent albuminuria can indicate damage to the glomerular filtration barrier, which normally restricts large plasma proteins.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After collecting ducts carry urine toward the papilla, which sequence correctly traces it toward the ureter?
questions.option_d: Renal papilla → calyx → renal pelvis → ureter
questions.explanation: Urine drains from collecting ducts at renal papillae into calyces, then the renal pelvis, and finally the ureter.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A waste product formed largely by normal muscle creatine metabolism is measured to estimate kidney filtration. Which substance is this?
questions.explanation: Creatinine is produced from creatine metabolism in muscle and is cleared largely by the kidneys, so blood levels help assess renal function.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which event initiates the micturition reflex when the urinary bladder fills?
questions.option_b: The liver releases bile into the bladder
questions.option_c: Stretch receptors in the bladder wall signal spinal reflex pathways
questions.option_d: The kidneys contract around the ureters
questions.explanation: Bladder-wall stretch receptors activate reflex pathways that coordinate detrusor contraction and sphincter control; voluntary centres can modulate urination.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A narrowing of the afferent arteriole reduces blood flow into a glomerulus. What is the usual immediate effect on glomerular filtration rate?
questions.option_a: It remains fixed because filtration is independent of pressure
questions.option_b: It becomes equal to urine flow in the ureter
questions.option_c: It falls as glomerular capillary pressure decreases
questions.option_d: It rises because less blood enters the kidney
questions.explanation: Afferent arteriolar constriction generally lowers glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and reduces GFR.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Reduced renal perfusion activates renin release from specialised kidney cells. Which downstream system is thereby engaged to help restore blood pressure and volume?
questions.explanation: Renin initiates the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system, which helps regulate vascular tone, sodium balance and blood pressure.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Severe loss of kidney filtration causes nitrogenous waste to accumulate in the blood. The clinical state is called:
questions.explanation: Uraemia describes the accumulation of urea and other nitrogenous wastes in blood in significant renal dysfunction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The ureter moves urine from the kidney toward the bladder even when a person is lying down. Which mechanism is important?
questions.option_a: Peristaltic contractions of ureter smooth muscle
questions.option_b: Skeletal muscle attached to each nephron
questions.explanation: Waves of smooth-muscle contraction propel urine through the ureters; transport does not depend solely on gravity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which structure temporarily stores urine and contracts during voiding?
questions.explanation: The urinary bladder is a distensible muscular reservoir that stores urine before it is expelled through the urethra.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient has painful frequent urination and inflammation primarily limited to the bladder. Which term best describes this infection?
questions.explanation: Cystitis is inflammation of the urinary bladder, commonly caused by infection.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A urine sample contains red blood cells. Which term describes this finding, without by itself establishing the cause?
questions.explanation: Haematuria means blood or red blood cells are present in urine; causes vary and require clinical assessment.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
